features.text: Patient reports high blood pressure, with a recent reading of 170/90 mmHg.
Patient experiences mild headaches when blood pressure is very high.
Patient denies shortness of breath, even with exertion.
Patient denies swelling in lower extremities except when standing for long periods.
Patient has a history of high blood pressure managed by a new PCP, with medication adjustments.
Patient is currently taking Norvasc 10 mg daily and Carvedilol 25 mg twice daily.
Patient previously took Lisinopril but has since discontinued it.
Patient occasionally uses nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like Advil or Motrin for knee or back pain.
Patient consumes a couple of beers during the week and one or two on weekends.
Patient's parents have a history of high blood pressure, and one parent had kidney disease.
Patient measures blood pressure at home using an electronic arm cuff, several times a week.
Patient is trying to improve diet but struggles during football season with high-calorie foods like pizza, wings, and subs.
Patient prefers to try a new restaurant with healthy options, such as salads, for better dietary choices.
Patient is open to working with the doctor to manage blood pressure and is hopeful for improvement.
Patient is willing to keep a record of blood pressure readings for the doctor's next visit.
Patient is aware of a local pharmacy (CVS) but has not been checking blood pressure there since the pandemic.
Patient is aware that a local pharmacy on Main Street has reopened for blood pressure checks.
